docs.title: must-tui Documentation
docs.text:
Welcome to the documentation for must-tui.

Use this site to find:

  • User Guide: install, configure, and use the terminal UI.
  • Developer Guide: set up a development environment and contribute.
  • API Reference: module-level documentation for the Python package.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: The API reference below is generated from source files in src/must_tui.

docs.title: PARAMETER_CACHE_MAX_AGE module-attribute
docs.text:
PARAMETER_CACHE_MAX_AGE = timedelta(days=1)

The parameter catalog is re-downloaded at startup only when the cache is older than this. Press 'r' to force it.

docs.title: HELP_KEYBINDINGS_PLACEHOLDER module-attribute
docs.text:
HELP_KEYBINDINGS_PLACEHOLDER = '<!-- KEYBINDINGS -->'

Marker in the bundled help.md replaced with a table generated from MUSTApp.BINDINGS.

Keeping the table generated (rather than hand-written in help.md) means it can't drift from the actual bindings: there is exactly one place (MUSTApp.BINDINGS) that defines what a key does.

docs.title: SEARCH_DEBOUNCE module-attribute
docs.text:
SEARCH_DEBOUNCE = 0.15

Seconds to wait after the last keystroke before searching, so typing a word searches once instead of per key.

docs.title: SEARCH_CHUNK_SIZE module-attribute
docs.text:
SEARCH_CHUNK_SIZE = 4096

Number of options scored per rapidfuzz call; each call blocks the UI thread until it returns (a few ms).

docs.title: SearchFields module-attribute
docs.text:
SearchFields = tuple[str, str, str, str]

The option label, MIB name, the label's bracketed description, and PCF description_2 of one parameter.

The bracketed description is also a substring of the label ("{mib_name} [{description}]"), but as its own, separately-anchorable field: an anchored regex like ^NC01_FRAME can otherwise never match it, since ^ on the label only ever matches at the mib_name's position (position 0), not at the bracket's.

docs.title: PLOT_DATE_FORM module-attribute
docs.text:
PLOT_DATE_FORM = 'Y-m-d H:M:S'

plotext date format matching format_datetime(), for Plot.date_form() / Plot.xlim().

docs.title: PLOT_COLORS module-attribute
docs.text:
PLOT_COLORS = ('blue+', 'green+', 'red+', 'cyan+', 'magenta+', 'orange+', 'gray+', 'blue', 'green', 'red', 'cyan', 'magenta', 'orange', 'gray')

Colors cycled across plotted series in the TUI plot; the first five match plotext's own default order. Deliberately excludes black/white, which can blend into the background. Names must be ones plotext.colorize() accepts (see plotext._dict.color_codes); it has no yellow or gold, unlike plotext's own default sequence.

docs.title: ParameterMetadata
docs.text:
ParameterMetadata()

Bases: Static

Widget to display metadata about a selected parameter.

The metadata information is obtained from the MUST server and consists of:

  • Description: parameter mnemonic
  • Data Type: one of UNSIGNED_SMALL_INT, ...
  • First Sample: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'
  • Last Sample: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS
  • Subsystem: one of TM, ...
  • Id:
  • Unit:
  • Parameter Type:
  • Name: mib name
  • Provider: name of the data provider

Also shows plotted-samples, the number of data points fetched for the parameter's current plot. This is computed locally (not provided by MUST) and is reset to "–" whenever a new parameter is selected.

set_sample_count(count: int | None) -> None

Show how many samples were fetched for the parameter's current plot, or "–" while that's unknown.

docs.title: ParameterInfo
docs.text:
ParameterInfo()

Bases: Static

Widget to display information about a selected parameter.

The information is obtained from the PCF file of the MIB and consists of:

  • description: parameter mnemonic
  • description_2: extended description
  • pid: On-board ID of the telemetry parameter
  • unit: Engineering unit mnemonic
  • ptc: Parameter Type Code
  • pfc: Parameter Format Code
  • width: Bit width of the parameter
  • valid: Validity flag
  • related: Related parameters
  • categ: Category of the parameter
  • natur: Nature of the parameter
  • curtx: Current telemetry index
  • inter: Interpretation
  • uscon: User context
  • decim: Decimation factor
  • parval: Parameter value
  • subsys: Subsystem
  • valpar: Validity parameter
  • sptype: Special type
  • corr: Correlation
  • obtid: On-board telemetry identifier
  • darc: Data archive
  • endian: Endianness

docs.title: search_options async
docs.text:
search_options(search: str, mode: str, generation: int) -> None

Search the ~70k options on a thread, so typing stays responsive.

Being exclusive, every keystroke cancels the previous search while it is still waiting out the debounce. A search that is already running on the thread can't be stopped, so its result is dropped when the search text, the mode or the catalog changed in the meantime. option_list.loading (set by the caller before this worker starts) covers the debounce + match time with a spinner, so typing doesn't look like it did nothing -- the combined delay (debounce plus the regex/fuzzy match itself) is small but not instant.

generation guards against a race on that shared loading flag: if this worker is cancelled, its finally can still run after a newer keystroke has already started a new worker and set loading back to True, since cancellation only takes effect at the next await, not synchronously. Clearing loading only when generation is still the latest one avoids an old, superseded worker turning the spinner off for a search that is still in progress.

docs.title: match_options
docs.text:
match_options(search: str, fields: list[SearchFields], mode: str) -> list[int]

Return the indices into fields that match search.

Modes:

  • "regex": all options where the case-insensitive regex matches one of the fields, in list order. Raises re.error for an invalid pattern.
  • "fuzzy": at most MAX_FUZZY_MATCHES options scoring above FUZZY_MIN_SCORE, best first.
  • "jump": the single best-scoring option (the first one when scores tie), or nothing for an empty list.

The fuzzy score of an option is the highest partial_ratio over its fields, rounded like thefuzz does. This is a pure function, so it can run on a worker thread.

docs.title: colored_plot_title
docs.text:
colored_plot_title(labels: list[str]) -> str

Like plot_title(), but each parameter name is colored (ANSI) to match its plotted series.

For a repeated label, the color of its first occurrence is used, matching the color replot() gives that series (by series_color() on the same index). TUI only: the Matplotlib backend has a real legend and keeps the plain plot_title().

docs.title: REQUEST_TIMEOUT module-attribute
docs.text:
REQUEST_TIMEOUT = ClientTimeout(total=None, sock_connect=30, sock_read=30)

Timeout for MUST link API requests: give up when connecting, or waiting for the next data, takes longer than 30 s.

There is no limit on the total duration, so large but healthy transfers still complete. aiohttp's default (5 minutes total) made the TUI look hung when the server stalled.

docs.title: PAGE_SIZE module-attribute
docs.text:
PAGE_SIZE = 5000

Samples requested per page from the paginated parameter data endpoint (its limit parameter).

MUST link's REST API doesn't document a maximum for limit, so this is a guess, not a confirmed safe value. If the server caps it lower, pagination still works correctly (the cursor is followed regardless of how many samples an actual page turns out to hold) -- it would just mean more, smaller pages than expected.

docs.title: MAX_PAGINATION_PAGES module-attribute
docs.text:
MAX_PAGINATION_PAGES = 1000

Safety limit on the number of pages get_parameter_data() follows via the paginated endpoint, guarding only against a runaway cursor (e.g. a server bug that never returns an empty one) -- not a limit MUST link documents or imposes itself. Deliberately generous (PAGE_SIZE * MAX_PAGINATION_PAGES == 5,000,000 samples at the current PAGE_SIZE): a flight telemetry series should never be silently truncated for a realistic query.

login(config_file: Path | None = None)

Login to MUST link with credentials from configuration.

Base URL, username, and password are first read from MUST_LINK_BASE_URL, MUST_LINK_USERNAME, and MUST_LINK_PASSWORD. If unset, values from the config file are used.

docs.title: search_parameters_async async
docs.text:
search_parameters_async(name_pattern: str, data_provider: str | None = None, ctx: MustContext | None = None, use_cache: bool = True) -> list[NavigableDict]

Search for parameters matching a pattern, returning all available metadata.

Returns a list of NavigableDict entries merging MUST server fields and PCF/MIB fields. MUST fields use snake_case keys (e.g. first_sample, data_type). PCF/MIB fields are all prefixed with pcf_ (e.g. pcf_description_2, pcf_unit).

The result is compatible with pd.DataFrame(result) and supports attribute access on individual items (e.g. result[0].first_sample).

docs.title: get_parameter_data async
docs.text:
get_parameter_data(ctx: MustContext, data_provider: str, par_name: str, start: str, end: str, paginated: bool = False, truncated: list[bool] | None = None)

Retrieve parameter data for a parameter from a data provider within a specified time range.

The dictionary has the following structure:

  • content: A list of dictionaries with the following keys:

    • monitoringChecks: None or a dictionary of monitoring checks
    • metadata: A list with parameter metadata as a dictionary: id, name, description, subsystem, dataType,type, complete, unit

    • data: A list of dictionaries with the following keys:

      • date (str): Timestamp in milliseconds since epoch
      • value (int): Raw value
      • calibratedValue (float): Calibrated value or 'N/A'

  • cursor: The cursor for pagination, empty string if no more data is available.

The plain (non-paginated) endpoint has no limit parameter of its own -- MUST link's REST API only accepts limit/cursor on .../data/paginated -- so limit is only sent when paginated is True.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default ctx MustContext

The MUST link context.

required data_provider str

The name of the data provider to retrieve data from.

required par_name str

The name of the parameter to retrieve data for.

required start str

The start time in 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' format.

required end str

The end time in 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' format.

required paginated bool

Whether to retrieve data in a paginated manner.

False truncated list[bool] | None

If given (only meaningful when paginated is True), True is appended to it when the MAX_PAGINATION_PAGES safety limit was reached while more data was still available (the cursor was non-empty), so the caller knows the returned data is incomplete.

None

Returns:

Type Description

A dictionary containing the parameter data.

Example:

{
    "content": [
        {
            "monitoringChecks": {
                "requiredSamples": 0,
                "useCalibrated": true,
                "checkInterpretation": "REAL",
                "checkDefinitions": [
                    {
                        "position": 0,
                        "type": "SOFT",
                        "lowValue": "string",
                        "highValue": "string",
                        "checkParameter": "string",
                        "checkValue": 0
                    }
                ]
            },
            "metadata": [
                {
                    "key": "string",
                    "value": "string"
                }
            ],
            "data": [
                {
                    "date": "string",
                    "value": 0,
                    "calibratedValue": "string"
                }
            ]
        }
    ],
    "cursor": "string"
}

docs.title: Developer Guide
docs.text: This section contains the basic developer workflow.

docs.title: Local setup
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/IvS-KULeuven/must-tui
cd must-tui
uv venv
source .venv/bin/activate
uv sync --extra docs

docs.title: Run the app
docs.text: must-tui

docs.title: Build docs
docs.text: uv run mkdocs serve

docs.title: Publish docs (local deploy)
docs.text:
Publish to GitHub Pages using the local MkDocs deploy command:

uv run mkdocs gh-deploy --remote-name upstream --remote-branch gh-pages --force

This pushes the generated site to the gh-pages branch of the upstream remote (IvS-KULeuven/must-tui), not your fork. See RELEASE.md in the repository root for the full release steps.

docs.title: Package docs dependencies only
docs.text: uv sync --extra docs

docs.title: Environment settings
docs.text: See the dedicated environment documentation in Environment, including variable meanings, fallback behavior, and setup examples.

docs.title: Environment Configuration
docs.text: This page describes environment variables used by must-tui, how they are resolved, and practical setup examples.

docs.title: Supported environment variables
docs.text:
must-tui uses the following environment variables:

  • MUST_LINK_BASE_URL: Base URL of the MUST link server.
  • MUST_LINK_USERNAME: Username used for authentication.
  • MUST_LINK_PASSWORD: Password used for authentication.
  • VERBOSE_DEBUG: Optional debug toggle (1 enables verbose debug logs).
  • XDG_CACHE_HOME: Root directory for cache files.

XDG stands for Cross-Desktop Group. XDG_CACHE_HOME is part of the XDG Base Directory Specification, which defines standard locations for user-specific files such as cache, configuration, and data.

docs.title: Resolution behavior
docs.text:
Credential lookup behavior:

  1. Read from environment variables.
  2. If missing, fall back to the config file: the path given with --config, or ~/.config/must-tui/config.json by default.

Each value is resolved on its own, so you can, for example, set the password as an environment variable and keep the base URL and username in the config file.

The config file uses its own lowercase keys, not the environment variable names:

Environment variable Config file key MUST_LINK_BASE_URL base_url MUST_LINK_USERNAME username MUST_LINK_PASSWORD password

The config file also accepts two optional keys that have no environment variable:

  • connect_timeout: connection timeout in seconds when logging in (default 30).
  • token: a MUST link token that is used when the login request fails.

Cache database location:

  • If XDG_CACHE_HOME is set:
  • $XDG_CACHE_HOME/must-tui/parameters.sqlite3
  • If XDG_CACHE_HOME is not set:
  • ~/.cache/must-tui/parameters.sqlite3

docs.title: Example: temporary shell session
docs.text:
export MUST_LINK_BASE_URL="https://must.example.org"
export MUST_LINK_USERNAME="flight-user"
export MUST_LINK_PASSWORD="change-me"
export VERBOSE_DEBUG=1
export XDG_CACHE_HOME="$HOME/.cache"

uv run must-tui

docs.title: Example: add to your shell profile
docs.text:
Add these lines to ~/.zshrc (or equivalent shell profile):

export MUST_LINK_BASE_URL="https://must.example.org"
export MUST_LINK_USERNAME="flight-user"
export XDG_CACHE_HOME="$HOME/.cache"

Then reload your shell:

source ~/.zshrc

Note: prefer entering secrets securely at runtime or through a secure secrets manager instead of storing passwords in shell profile files.

docs.title: Example: config-file fallback
docs.text:
If environment variables are not provided, create ~/.config/must-tui/config.json:

{
  "base_url": "https://must.example.org",
  "username": "flight-user",
  "password": "change-me"
}

Use the lowercase keys shown above. Keys named after the environment variables (such as "MUST_LINK_BASE_URL") are ignored in the config file.

docs.title: Example: custom cache location
docs.text:
export XDG_CACHE_HOME="$HOME/work-cache"
uv run must-tui

With this configuration, cache will be stored at:

$HOME/work-cache/must-tui/parameters.sqlite3

docs.title: Quick checks
docs.text:
Verify variables in the current shell:

env | grep -E 'MUST_LINK|VERBOSE_DEBUG|XDG_CACHE_HOME'

Check where the cache file should be:

echo "${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/must-tui/parameters.sqlite3"

docs.title: Using the TUI
docs.text:
The MUST TUI launches in a terminal and provides interactive access to telemetry parameters, their metadata, and time-series plots.

Press F1 at any time for an in-app help screen covering usage and the full list of keyboard shortcuts — the same reference as the Global Key Bindings section below, generated from the app's own bindings so the two can't drift apart.

docs.title: Search Input
docs.text:
The search box at the top filters or navigates the parameter list as you type.

  • Filter mode (default): The list is narrowed down to parameters whose name or description match the search text. By default the search text is treated as a regular expression. Uncheck the Regex checkbox to switch to fuzzy matching instead.
  • Jump mode: The best fuzzy match is highlighted in the alphabetically sorted list, with up to 500 neighbouring parameters shown around it. Toggle jump mode with Ctrl+J.

The Regex checkbox (top-right of the search bar) switches between regex and fuzzy matching while in filter mode.

The search checks the MIB name, the description shown in brackets in the list, and the MUST/PCF extended description — each as its own field, so an anchored pattern like ^NC01_FRAME matches the bracketed description directly, not just where it happens to sit inside the full list entry.

The search runs once you pause typing for a moment, not on every keystroke, and a spinner covers the parameter list while it's running. While a regular expression is incomplete or invalid (e.g. an unclosed parenthesis), the list keeps showing the previous matches.

docs.title: Parameter List
docs.text:
The left panel lists all parameters retrieved from the MUST server for the configured data provider. Each entry is shown as:

MIBNAME [Description]

To keep the interface responsive, the list shows at most 500 parameters at a time out of however many currently match. When there are more, the last entry reports how many are left out; select it (or press Enter while it's highlighted) to load all of them — this can take a few seconds for a very large, unfiltered list — or refine the search instead to narrow it down.

Scroll through the list with the arrow keys or the mouse. Press Enter (or click) to select a parameter — this loads its MIB info, server metadata, and time-series data into the other panels. Server data is loaded in the background, so the interface stays responsive. If you select another parameter before the previous one has finished loading, the previous request is cancelled and only the latest selection is loaded. A request is abandoned, and reported in a dialog, when the MUST server sends no data for 30 seconds; slow transfers that keep receiving data are not interrupted.

docs.title: Parameter Info
docs.text:
The upper-centre panel shows technical details read from the PCF file of the MIB for the selected parameter.

Field Description par_name MIB parameter name description Short mnemonic description description_2 Extended description pid On-board identifier of the telemetry parameter unit Engineering unit mnemonic decim Number of decimal places to be used for displaying real values of this monitoring parameter ptc Parameter Type Code pfc Parameter Format Code width 'Padded' width of this parameter expressed in number of bits valid Name of the parameter to be used to determine the state validity of the parameter specified in this record related Name of monitoring parameter categ Calibration category: N=numeric, S=status, T=text natur Nature of the parameter: R=raw, D=dynamic OL, H=hardcoded, S=save synthetic, C=constant curtx Parameter calibration identification name inter Flag controlling extrapolation behavior uscon parval Raw value for a constant parameter subsys valpar Raw value for a validity parameter sptype corr Flag that controls correlation of absolute time parameters obtid OBT ID darc endian Endianness: 'B' or 'L'

docs.title: Parameter Metadata
docs.text:
The upper-right panel shows live metadata fetched from the MUST server for the selected parameter.

Field Description description Parameter mnemonic from the server data-type Data type (e.g. UNSIGNED_SMALL_INT) first-sample Timestamp of the earliest available sample last-sample Timestamp of the most recent available sample subsystem Subsystem (e.g. TM) id Internal parameter identifier unit Engineering unit parameter-type Parameter type name MIB name provider Data provider name plotted-samples Number of data points fetched for the current plot; – while unknown (computed locally, not from MUST)

docs.title: Plot Controls
docs.text:
A toolbar between the info panels and the plot area:

Control Action Clear Plot button Remove all plotted traces Plot: TUI / Plot: Matplotlib button Toggle between the built-in TUI plot and an external Matplotlib window Data Range button Set the time range to the selected parameter's first and last sample, as reported by MUST Y Range button Set an explicit Y-axis minimum and maximum, or go back to auto-scaling Start → End fields Set the start and end time for data retrieval and the plot x-axis Lock checkbox Keep the duration fixed: changing one end moves the other end along

By default the Y-axis auto-scales to fit whatever is currently plotted. The Y Range button opens a small dialog with Min and Max fields (pre-filled with the currently plotted data's range, or the active locked range if one is set) and three actions: Apply (validates that Min is less than Max), Auto (clears the locked range immediately), and Cancel. Once a range is locked, it stays in effect — across new parameter selections, time range reloads, and clearing the plot — until you choose Auto again, for both the TUI and Matplotlib backends.

Type a date-time as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. Shorter forms are accepted too: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (seconds 0) and YYYY-MM-DD (midnight). A field is applied when you press Enter or leave it (e.g. with Tab); typing alone changes nothing. Escape leaves the field, committing a pending valid edit first, the same as Tab.

Relative forms are also accepted, resolved against the current local time:

  • now, today, yesterday, tomorrow — today/yesterday/tomorrow snap to local midnight; now keeps the current time, to the second.
  • Any of those with a signed offset, e.g. now-6h, tomorrow+1d, yesterday-3h. The offset uses weeks, days, hours, minutes and seconds, and they can be combined: now-1d2h30m.
  • A bare offset such as -2h30m or +1w is relative to now. The sign is required (6h alone is rejected as ambiguous).

↑ / ↓ step the date-time component the cursor is on (year, month, day, hour, minute, second) up or down by one, directly in the field's text — without applying it, so pending edits are still only applied on Enter/Tab/Escape. Stepping a relative expression first resolves it to an absolute date-time, then steps it. Stepping the day/month clamps to the last valid day of the resulting month (e.g. 31 Jan + 1 month → 28 Feb); stepping past year 1000 or 9999 does nothing.

If the text is not a valid date-time, or the start would not be before the end, the field turns red, a notification explains why, and the time range stays as it was. Editing the field removes the red mark.

When the time range changes, the x-axis moves to the new range and all plotted parameters are fetched again for it. A notification shows when the reload starts and when it is done; parameters without data in the new range are listed there and removed from the plot. Selecting a parameter fetches and plots its data for the current time range.

docs.title: Plot
docs.text:
The lower-right area renders a time-series plot of the selected parameter(s). Multiple parameters can be overlaid — each new selection adds a trace without clearing previous ones. The title lists every currently plotted parameter (Parameter: X for one, Parameters: X, Y, … for several), each one colored to match its trace. The Matplotlib backend shows a real legend instead; a legend in the TUI plot can crash the terminal plotting library in some situations, so the title's coloring is used there instead.

To keep the terminal plot fast, each trace is drawn with at most 1000 points. Long series are reduced by keeping the minimum and maximum of each time bucket, so spikes and dips remain visible. The Matplotlib backend always shows the full-resolution data.

Fetching a parameter with many samples in the selected time range can take a while — data is retrieved page by page (5000 samples per request, over one reused connection, to avoid one huge request to the MUST server), and all of it is retrieved before anything is drawn. A spinner covers the plot area while a selection or a time range change is being fetched, and the Parameter Metadata panel's plotted-samples field shows the resulting point count once it's done. If a single parameter's data in the selected range is extremely large (over 5,000,000 samples), a notification reports that only the first part of it was loaded.

Use the Clear Plot button (or press Ctrl+L) to reset the plot.

The plot marker style can be cycled through four options (Braille, Standard Definition, High Definition, Dot) with F3.

docs.title: Global Key Bindings
docs.text:
These bindings are available anywhere in the application. Every one of them is a Ctrl-combo or a function key — none are bare letters, so none are ever swallowed by the search box as typed text, regardless of where focus is:

Key Action F1 Open this help Ctrl+Q Quit the application Ctrl+L Clear all traces from the plot Ctrl+Z Maximize the plot and its controls, hiding everything else; press again to restore Ctrl+J Toggle between Filter and Jump search mode F2 Toggle plot backend between TUI (built-in) and Matplotlib F3 Cycle plot marker style (Braille → SD → HD → Dot) F4 Toggle light / dark mode F5 Soft-refresh the parameter cache (fetches from server, keeps SQLite cache) Ctrl+R Hard-reset the parameter cache (wipes SQLite cache, then re-fetches)

Only the first four (F1, Ctrl+Q, Ctrl+L, Ctrl+Z) are shown in the footer, to keep it short; the rest still work exactly the same, they're just not advertised there. The full table — generated from the same bindings the app actually uses, so it can't go out of date — is always available by pressing F1.

The status line above the footer shows the data provider, connection state, the number of parameters currently loaded, and how long ago the parameter cache was last refreshed.

docs.title: Loading Screen
docs.text:
On startup the app shows a loading screen while it:

  1. Authenticates with the MUST server.
  2. Loads MIB parameter info from the bundled pcf.dat.
  3. Fetches the parameter catalog.

If authentication fails the app offers the choice to Abort or continue in offline mode (no server data, MIB browsing only).

docs.title: Main Screen
docs.text: After loading, the main screen is shown with the parameter list. The parameter catalog is loaded from the local SQLite cache when available. A background refresh from the server runs at startup only when the cache is missing or older than one day; press F5 to refresh it at any time.

docs.title: TUI (default)
docs.text: The built-in Textual plot renders directly in the terminal. No graphical session is required.

docs.title: Matplotlib
docs.text: Requires a graphical desktop session with a window manager. When enabled, an external Matplotlib window opens alongside the terminal and stays in sync with the time range and parameter selections. Switch back to the TUI backend with F2 or the Plot: TUI button.

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text: This section describes how to install and run must-tui.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: uv tool install must-tui

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
must-tui

Pass --config to use a config file at a non-default location:

must-tui --config /path/to/my-config.json

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The application reads MUST link connection settings from environment variables with precedence over the config file.

Configuration precedence:

  1. Environment variables
  2. The config file

Only one config file is read: the one given with --config <path>, or ~/.config/must-tui/config.json when --config is not used. The default file is not consulted as a further fallback when --config is given.

Supported environment variables:

  • MUST_LINK_BASE_URL
  • MUST_LINK_USERNAME
  • MUST_LINK_PASSWORD

If any required value is missing from both sources, login fails with an error.

Example config file:

{
    "base_url": "https://mustlink.example.org",
    "username": "your-username",
    "password": "your-password",
    "connect_timeout": 30,
    "token": "optional-fallback-token"
}

Example environment-based setup:

export MUST_LINK_BASE_URL="https://mustlink.example.org"
export MUST_LINK_USERNAME="your-username"
export MUST_LINK_PASSWORD="your-password"
must-tui

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The tool requires network access to the MUST backend.
  • Authentication must be configured in your runtime environment.

docs.title: Python REPL Helpers
docs.text:
The must_tui.must module provides two helper functions that are useful from a Python REPL or scripts.

In a notebook, prefer the async helpers with await when you can:

from must_tui.must import get_parameter_names_async

matches = await get_parameter_names_async(
  name_pattern="nc12.*tsense",
  data_provider="PLATO",
  use_cache=True,
)

The synchronous wrappers, such as get_parameter_names() and get_parameter_series(), are still available for plain scripts and will also work in notebooks through an internal bridge.

docs.title: get_parameter_names()
docs.text:
Use this function to search parameter names and descriptions.

from must_tui.must import get_parameter_names

matches = get_parameter_names(
    name_pattern="nc12.*tsense",
    data_provider="PLATO",
    use_cache=True,
)

for name, description in matches.items():
    print(name, "-", description)

Arguments:

  • name_pattern (str): Case-insensitive regex pattern. If the regex is invalid, the value is treated as a literal string.
  • data_provider (str | None): Optional provider name. If omitted, all available providers are searched.
  • use_cache (bool): When True (default), searches the local parameter catalog cache for faster lookups.

Returns:

  • dict[str, str]: Mapping of parameter name to description.

docs.title: search_parameters()
docs.text:
Use this function to search parameters and retrieve all available metadata in one call — richer than get_parameter_names() because it returns structured records instead of a plain name-to-description mapping.

from must_tui.must import search_parameters
import pandas as pd

results = search_parameters(
    name_pattern="nc12.*tsense",
    data_provider="PLATO",
    use_cache=True,
)

# Each result is a NavigableDict — supports attribute access
for rec in results:
    print(rec.name, rec.first_sample, rec.pcf_unit)

# Compatible with pandas
df = pd.DataFrame(results)
print(df[["name", "description", "first_sample", "last_sample", "pcf_description_2"]])

Arguments:

  • name_pattern (str): Case-insensitive regex pattern matched against parameter name, MUST description, and PCF description_2. If the regex is invalid, the value is treated as a literal string.
  • data_provider (str | None): Optional provider name. If omitted, all available providers are searched.
  • use_cache (bool): When True (default), searches the local parameter catalog cache for faster lookups.

Returns:

  • list[NavigableDict]: List of records sorted by parameter name. Each record contains:
  • MUST server fields in snake_case (e.g. name, description, data_type, first_sample, last_sample, unit, provider)
  • PCF/MIB fields prefixed with pcf_ (e.g. pcf_description_2, pcf_unit, pcf_ptc)

The async counterpart search_parameters_async() accepts the same arguments plus an optional ctx (MustContext).

docs.title: get_parameter_series()
docs.text:
Use this function to retrieve one or more parameter time series.

from datetime import datetime
from must_tui.must import get_parameter_series

series = get_parameter_series(
    parameter_names=["CNLA1022", "CNLA1023"],
    data_provider="PLATO",
    start=datetime(2025, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0),
    end=datetime(2026, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0),
)

for par_name, samples in series.items():
    print(par_name, len(samples), "samples")

Arguments:

  • parameter_names (str | list[str]): One parameter name or a list of names.
  • data_provider (str): Provider name used for data retrieval.
  • start (str | datetime | None): Optional start time.
  • end (str | datetime | None): Optional end time.
  • ctx (MustContext | None): Optional authenticated context.

If start and end are omitted, the helper uses metadata bounds (first-sample and last-sample) per parameter.

Returns:

  • dict[str, list[tuple[datetime, float | int]]]: Mapping of parameter name to (timestamp, value) samples.
